subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What are the three basic processes involved in memory?
questions.explain: Memory works by encoding information in, storing it, and later retrieving it.

questions.q: According to Miller, what is the typical capacity of short-term memory?
questions.explain: Miller's 'magic number' suggests STM holds about 5 to 9 (7±2) items.

questions.q: Roughly how long can information be held in short-term memory without rehearsal?
questions.explain: Without rehearsal, STM information fades after about 18 to 30 seconds.

questions.q: What is the accepted capacity of long-term memory?
questions.explain: Long-term memory is thought to have a potentially unlimited capacity.

questions.q: Who proposed the multi-store model of memory in 1968?
questions.explain: The multi-store model was put forward by Atkinson and Shiffrin in 1968.

questions.q: Which psychologist proposed the theory of reconstructive memory?
questions.explain: Bartlett proposed that memory is an active, reconstructive process.

questions.q: Which story did Bartlett famously use to investigate reconstructive memory?
questions.explain: Bartlett used the Native American folk tale 'The War of the Ghosts' in his research.

questions.q: Which patient is the focus of the OCR core study on memory by Wilson, Kopelman and Kapur?
questions.explain: The core study investigates the amnesic musician Clive Wearing.

questions.q: In which year was the Wilson, Kopelman and Kapur study of Clive Wearing published?
questions.explain: The core study on Clive Wearing by Wilson, Kopelman and Kapur was published in 2008.

questions.q: According to research, short-term memory mainly encodes information in which form?
questions.explain: STM tends to encode information acoustically, whereas LTM is largely semantic.

questions.q: In the multi-store model, what allows information to pass from sensory memory into short-term memory?
questions.explain: Paying attention to sensory information transfers it into short-term memory.

questions.q: In the multi-store model, what process transfers information from short-term to long-term memory?
questions.explain: Maintenance rehearsal moves information from STM into LTM.

questions.q: In reconstructive memory theory, what is a 'schema'?
options: A mental framework of prior knowledge and expectations
A brain region that stores memories
questions.explain: Schemas are packages of prior knowledge that shape how we reconstruct memories.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes encoding from storage?
options: Encoding changes information into a usable form, while storage holds it over time
Encoding retrieves information, while storage deletes it
Encoding holds information, while storage changes its form
They are two words for exactly the same process
questions.explain: Encoding converts information into a form that can be held, and storage maintains it.

questions.q: What caused the severe brain damage that led to Clive Wearing's amnesia?
options: A stroke caused by high blood pressure
A blow to the head in an accident
A genetic disorder present from birth
questions.explain: A herpes viral infection caused encephalitis that damaged brain areas including the hippocampus.

questions.q: Which ability did Clive Wearing surprisingly retain despite his profound amnesia?
options: The ability to play the piano and conduct music
The ability to form detailed new memories
A full memory of his earlier life
The ability to learn new people's names
questions.explain: His procedural memory was largely intact, so he could still play and conduct music.

questions.q: Which is a common criticism of the multi-store model of memory?
options: It is too simple and treats STM and LTM as single, unitary stores
It ignores the role of encoding entirely
It claims memory has no capacity limits
It was never supported by any evidence
questions.explain: The model is criticised for oversimplifying memory, as STM and LTM appear to have several components.

questions.q: Jamal repeats a new phone number to himself over and over until he can dial it. Which process is he using?
questions.explain: Repeating information to keep it available is maintenance rehearsal.

questions.q: A witness confidently recalls seeing a knife at a scene where there was none, matching her idea of a 'robbery'. This best illustrates which idea?
options: Memory is reconstructive and shaped by schemas
Short-term memory has a limited capacity
Memory is a perfect recording of events
questions.explain: Her schema for a robbery has distorted her memory, showing reconstructive memory.

questions.q: Like Clive Wearing, a patient cannot form any new long-term memories after his illness, forgetting events within seconds. This is best described as which type of amnesia?
questions.explain: An inability to form new memories after brain damage is anterograde amnesia.
